label: Poster Canvas
description: Typography-first Next.js starter that treats the first page as a poster. For experiments and art-directed one-pagers when the prompt wants a statement, not a blank app.
signatureMotif: one oversized poster line, empty canvas, and a single quiet action
promptHints: The first route is a poster: one huge line, lots of empty canvas, one small action. Do not lay out a product landing with feature cards.
Keep Next.js starter structure. Visual energy lives in type and space, not in extra sections.
If the user later asks for an app, grow from this poster — do not suddenly switch to a mint dashboard.

layouts: Home is min-h-screen with a single headline at clamp(4rem, 12vw, 9rem), flush left or slightly off-center, and a short line + one text link or button under it. The rest of the viewport stays empty.
If a second block is needed, it is a thin footer strip: year, name, one social — not a 3-column starter feature grid.
Do not invent pricing, testimonials, or a product screenshot. This scaffold is a canvas.
Mobile stacks the same poster tighter; never introduce cards to fill space.
motifs: Paper or bone background, ink type, one accent only if the prompt names a color.
Fraunces or Space Grotesk for the poster line; Inter/Manrope for the small line.
No gradients, no noise textures, no glass. The empty space is the design.
antiPatterns: Do not render starter-neutral or playground-mono chrome: dark IDE shell, mono playground, or extension-first empty app frames.
Avoid fresh-mint teal product cards and studio-soft designer dashboards.
No 3-up Getting started cards, counter widgets, or template-looking hero+features.
